title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of drift-diffusion process under threshold resetting
authors: Rahul Das, Satya N Majumdar, Arnab Pal
abstract: We study the emergence of non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) in stochastic processes under threshold resetting, an event-driven protocol in which the system resets to its initial configuration upon crossing a prescribed spatial boundary (threshold). In contrast to externally driven resetting, whose steady-state properties are well understood, the behavior under threshold resetting remains largely unexplored. We derive general conditions for the existence of a NESS and show that, whenever it exists, the steady state at a given position $x$ can be expressed as the ratio of two fundamental quantities: the mean local time (MLT) at $x$ and the mean first-passage time (MFPT) to hit the threshold. In particular, for noisy systems, a finite MFPT guarantees the existence of a NESS. As an illustrative example, we analyze a drift-diffusion process in one dimension and uncover rich intermediate-time dynamics, including anomalous relaxation in the spatial distribution, damped oscillations in the moments and in the mean-squared displacement (MSD), governed by system parameters. Our findings provide a general understanding of the emergence of non-equilibrium steady states and relaxation dynamics under threshold resetting, revealing how induced events shape the spatial and temporal properties of a broad class of stochastic processes.
summary: This paper develops a general theory for non-equilibrium steady states in stochastic processes that undergo threshold resetting. By analyzing the drift-diffusion model, the authors derive that the steady-state distribution depends on the ratio of the mean local time to the mean first-passage time. The work provides deep insights into how boundary-induced events shape the long-term spatial and temporal behavior of physical systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) and the relaxation dynamics of stochastic processes subjected to threshold resetting.
main_result: The NESS distribution is found to be proportional to the ratio of the Mean Local Time (MLT) to the Mean First-Passage Time (MFPT). The analysis also reveals rich intermediate-time dynamics, including anomalous relaxation and damped oscillations.
method: The authors employ a renewal formalism and Laplace transformation techniques to derive general conditions for NESS existence and analyze the propagator $P(x, t|x_0)$.
model_or_system: The primary model is a general stochastic process, specifically analyzed using a one-dimensional drift-diffusion process. The process is characterized by resetting to the initial configuration upon crossing a predefined spatial boundary (the threshold).
key_observables: Non-Equilibrium Steady State (NESS) distribution, Mean Local Time (MLT), Mean First-Passage Time (MFPT), Mean-Square Displacement (MSD), and the probability propagator $P(x, t|x_0)$.
important_parameters: The Péclet number ($Pe = x_0 v / (2D)$) governs the relative importance of advection versus diffusion, defining different dynamical regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the reset event is instantaneous upon reaching the threshold, and the general framework relies on the existence of a finite MFPT to guarantee a NESS.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the threshold resetting process on a semi-infinite line. Other figures likely detail the mathematical structure of the propagator or the resulting steady-state profiles.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general theoretical framework for NESS under threshold resetting. It then applies this formalism to the drift-diffusion process, deriving the steady-state solution using renewal equations and Laplace transforms. Finally, it analyzes the transient dynamics, including large-time asymptotics, for specific parameter regimes.
why_interesting: The theoretical framework developed for analyzing non-equilibrium steady states driven by boundary-induced events (threshold resetting) provides a general tool applicable to open quantum systems or quantum dynamics where dissipation or measurement-induced resets are present.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of threshold resetting on the semi-infinite line. A particle starts at x = x0 and evolves under its intrinsic dynamics until it reaches the threshold at the origin, where it is instantaneously reset to x0. Repeated threshold resetting events lead, at long times, to a stationary distribution Pss(x).

FIG. 2. Temporal evolution of the probability density P(x, t|x0) for a particle undergoing drift-diffusion (DD) subject to threshold resetting (TR). The panels illustrate two distinct Pe regimes: (a) diffusion-dominated regime (Pe = 0.05); (b) intermediate crossover regime (Pe = 1); the high Pe regime is discussed separately in Fig. 4. The dynamic approach to the non-equilibrium steady state (SS, solid red line) is shown for different times. Solid lines represent exact analytical solutions, whereas markers denote Monte Carlo simulation data. In both panels, the kink at x = x0 in the SS is clearly visible, as shown in Eq. (26) in terms of the discontinuity in the first spatial derivative....

FIG. 3. Verification of Eq. (26), regarding the jump discon- tinuity in the first derivative of the steady state at u = 1, is shown for various Pe with a slope of −2. Here, we change velocity v, keeping x0 and D fixed. System parameters: x0 = 1, D = 0.5, v ∈[0, 20].

FIG. 4. Temporal evolution of P(x, t|x0), and G+(x, t|x0) for Pe = 20, or drift-dominated regime. Each panel shows the propagator at different times. Comparing the above fig- ure with Eq. (27), we find that a peak near the origin at early times (t = 2, 3) arises due to the first (reset-free) term G+(x, t|x0). At later times, the reset-free contribution be- comes very small, and eventually it relaxes to the steady state (SS) due to multiple resetting events. The kink in the SS at x = x0 is visible in panel (d). The solid line is the analytical solution, and markers denote the simulation data. System parameters are: x0 = 10, v = 4, D = 1.

FIG. 5. Temporal evolution of Mean Square Displacement (MSD) and mean position for drift-diffusion under threshold resetting (TR). Panels (a) and (c) illustrate the oscillatory regime for mean position and MSD, respectively, using pa- rameters x0 = 10, v = 4, D = 1, i.e., Pe = 20. Panels (b) and (d) show the transition to non-oscillatory behavior when diffusion dominates, or drift is reduced. Parameters used: x0 = 10, v = 1, D = 6, i.e., Pe = 0.833. Solid lines represent the theory, while colored points denote simulation results.
